scope: Single-host factory runtime (K1 sandbox + host test services).
k1_note: Host-wide K1 run slots and per-lane slots. Enforced atomically by factory k1 before factory k1 up starts containers; a refusal is K1_SLOT_BUSY. See files/runbooks/k1.md and files/policies/dispatch-rules.json.

postgres.note: Single server-side cap for all three PostgreSQL containers. pg2a, pg2b and the K1 pg service all pass -c max_connections in their compose files; this value is the single declared cap. The app pool below is separate. The host pg services also carry a bounded work_mem so 100 connections cannot exhaust the 1 GB limit.

test_database.note: Every harness invocation names its own base database (factory_<token>), so Django and pytest-django derive distinct test_<name> databases and cannot create/drop each other's. A lane maps to its own server. DB-backed checks take one OS file-lock slot per server before starting, and wait for it instead of colliding; the lock dies with the process. PostgreSQL data is tmpfs, so a restarted server also discards any orphaned test database.

app.note: Documented application pool per Postgres service instance. At most three pools on this host (K1 app, pg2a, pg2b) use 30 of the 100 server connections; the remainder covers suite workers, concurrent-writer probes and reserved/admin slots. See files/runbooks/k1.md and files/runbooks/services.md.

probe.note: A probe is bounded by its runtime, not by one host number. SQLite is single-writer (cap 1): a concurrent-writer probe on it is an ENGINE_FAULT, not coverage. A K1 run has its own PostgreSQL and network, so it may use the catalog depth (up to 16 concurrent writers). A host PostgreSQL probe is capped at 8 so two lanes plus an ad-hoc run cannot exhaust one 100-connection server. The catalog's depth is the upper bound; this file never raises it.
